# Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0501a)

**ID:** Atk S0501a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Illustrator of Ultimate Meaning
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā*, also titled *Paramatthajotikā I*, is the Theravāda commentary on the *Khuddakapāṭha*, belonging to the Khuddakanikāya of the Pali canon [Karashima 2012; Phaengcharoen 2006]. In its opening verses, the author humbly claims to possess limited knowledge of the teaching and explains that he compiles the commentary relying upon the decisions of the former teachers (*pubbācariya-vinicchaya*) and the ancient decisions (*porāṇa-vinicchaya*) [Adikaram 1946]. This self-deprecating opening stands in tension with the closing verses (*nigamana*), which conversely praise the author's comprehensive mastery of the Dhamma, prompting scholarly discussion regarding the authorship and textual stratification of the work relative to Buddhaghosa's canonical commentaries [Dhammadinna 2014]. Furthermore, variations between commentaries—such as the full exposition of the opening narrative formula *evaṃ me sutaṃ* here, contrasted with the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* referring readers to the *Papañcasūdanī*—highlight distinct compositional treatments across the tradition [Adikaram 1946].

The commentary preserves specific doctrinal classifications and narrative glosses. It classifies arahants into two distinct categories: the "bare-insight worker" (*sukkhavipassaka*) and the practitioner whose vehicle is serenity (*samathayānika*) [Endo 1997]. In legendary accounts of the wheel-turning monarch (*cakkavatti*), the text describes the miraculous elephant jewel (*hatthi-ratana*), noting that it derives from either the Uposatha or Chaddanta elephant stock, characterized as entirely white (*sabbaseto*), possessing supernatural potency (*iddhimant*), and capable of flying through the air (*vehāsaṅgama*) [Endo 2002]. Lexically, the commentary is also cited for explaining architectural terms such as *dhātugabbha* as an inner relic chamber [Radich, Mahāparinirvāṇa-mahāsūtra].

The text was edited for the Pali Text Society by Helmer Smith in 1915 [Endo 1997; Masefield 1979], and translated into English by Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli under the title *The Illustrator of Ultimate Meaning* [Masefield 1979].

Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus shows that the commentary shares extensive Pali-internal material across 436 texts (more than 31,000 matches), with its most massive parallel reuse occurring in its companion commentary, the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* (*Paramatthajotikā II*), which contains over 2,000 matching passages with sequences reaching 97% similarity (e.g., §802_3–921 aligned with §1016_0–1114) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits large shared segments with the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Visuddhimagga*, the *Majjhima-nikāya* commentary (*Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*), the *Sīlakkhandhavagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vinaya* commentary (*Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with scores of 10 or above are identified [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0505a) (§802_3–921 ↔ §1016_0–1114); Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh02a) (§249_5–249_21 ↔ §1192_5–1193_12); Visuddhimaggo (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Anya E0101n) (§504_5–511_2 ↔ §1297_4–1305_0); Dasakanipāta (AN 10) (§980_0–984_3 ↔ §177.5.1_3–177.9.3); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§785_0–788_10 ↔ §1544_2–1548_10); Dīghanikāye Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā (Atk S0101a) (§474_0–484_3 ↔ §215_0–225_3); Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Vin01a) (§416_0–440_5 ↔ §76_1–99_8); Udāna-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0503a) (§524_0–526_1 ↔ §221_0–223_1)

**Sources**

- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Discusses the opening verses on pubbācariya-vinicchaya and porāṇa-vinicchaya, and differences with the Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā regarding evam me sutam.
- [Dhammadinna 2014] Dhammadinna, ed., Research on the Dīrgha-āgama (2014) — Discusses the contrast between the author's self-deprecating prologue and the concluding nigamana regarding authorship.
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Notes the classification of arahants into sukkhavipassaka and samathayānika, and cites Helmer Smith's PTS edition.
- [Endo 2002] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism (1997, 2002) — Documents the description of the cakkavatti's elephant jewel (hatthi-ratana) from Uposatha and Chaddanta breeds.
- [Karashima 2012] Seishi Karashima, Abhisamācārikā Dharmāḥ (2012) — Attests the equivalence between Paramatthajotikā I and Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Masefield 1979] Peter Masefield, Divine Revelation in Pali Buddhism (1979, 1994) — Provides bibliographic citations of Helmer Smith's PTS edition and Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli's English translation.
- [Phaengcharoen 2006] Phramaha Somphong Santacitto Phaengcharoen, Analytical Study of Concept of Dhamma as Natural Law in Theravada (2006) — Confirms the title Paramatthajotikā I and Helmer Smith's PTS edition.
- [Radich, Mahāparinirvāṇa-mahāsūtra] Michael Radich, The Mahāparinirvāṇa-mahāsūtra and the Emergence of Tathāgatagarbha Doctrine — Cites the commentary's gloss on dhātugabbha as an inner chamber or relic repository.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database — Provides automated text-reuse match statistics and passage alignments with Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā, Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā, Visuddhimagga, and other commentaries.
